Title: Not an antique, yet bearing traces of time
This is an ornament that instantly calms your mind.
Designed into vintage barrel beads with distinctive Tibetan style, its color naturally transitions from rich honey yellow to deep tea brown, as if polished meticulously by time. The striking natural crack lines covering the bead surface are marks left by years. It presents a mild, glossy and amber-like tranquil texture under light.
Design Essence: Visualize the Passage of Time
Inspired by ancient Tibetan beads steeped in ghee and tempered by centuries of time, this bracelet pursues not only classic shapes, but also the vintage charm passed down through generations. Rugged yet delicate, steady yet timeless, it embodies the boldness and devotion of Tibetan culture, as well as sophisticated modern aesthetics.
How It Brings Inner Peace
Amid hustle and bustle of daily trivialities, it acts as your spiritual anchor. It brings steady inner peace with no profound historical background required. It perfectly matches simple linen shirts and retro ethnic accessories, instantly enhancing your oriental charm. There is no need to chase definite results while playing with it. Simply slide the beads gently and embrace the tranquility flowing from fingertips to heart.
Maintenance Tips
Rub the beads softly with cotton cloth for several days after receipt. Once the glossy patina emerges, the bracelet will show more charming luster.

BAYELSA ASSEMBLY APPROVES REMOVAL OF SAGBAMA CHAIRMAN & VICE 
ANOTHER CASE OF EXECUTIVE OVERREACH?
WRITTEN BY: GREATMAN OATH 
BREAKING:
The Bayelsa State House of Assembly has approved the removal of the Chairman and Vice Chairman of Sagbama Local Government Area from office.
The resolution came after what the Assembly described as findings of financial misappropriation and maladministration_ against the council leadership.
WHAT WE KNOW:
1. The Pattern
This is not new in Bayelsa. Back in the Dickson era, the House also probed and recommended removal of chairmen of Brass, Southern Ijaw, Sagbama, Ogbia and Ekeremor over alleged financial misconduct.
2. The Process.
For 3 weeks, chairmen were grilled by lawmakers. Some could not defend expenditures or tender valid council documents.
The Governor at the time defended the action, saying he only acted on Assembly recommendations. 
3. Current Politics.
The Sagbama Chairman, Alice Tangi, was among LGA chairmen who were recently under pressure over party defection issues. The Deputy Governor, Lawrence Ewhrudjakpo, even sued the Assembly, alleging plans to impeach officials who refused to dump PDP.
 THE HARD TRUTH RIVERS & BAYELSA MUST FACE.
Let’s be honest. This is not just about Sagbama.
1. ABUSE OF POWER: LG AUTONOMY IS DEAD ON PAPER.
Section 7 of the Constitution guarantees LG autonomy. But in Bayelsa, LG Chairmen are removed like Branch Managers.
When the State Assembly "probes" and "recommends" and the Governor "acts", the question is: Who is really in charge?
LG money comes from Abuja, but the state decides who spends it. That’s not federalism. That’s feudalism.
2. FAILURE OF INSTITUTIONS.
For 3 weeks chairmen couldn’t defend spending or produce documents.
If that’s true, it’s a failure of leadership.
But if the probe is political — especially with the current PDP/APC defection drama — then it’s a failure of democracy.
You cannot use "financial misappropriation" as a cover to punish political disloyalty. 
3. THE SAGBAMA FACTOR.
Sagbama is the Governor’s LGA. It’s also the LGA being mentioned in the zoning debate for Deputy Governor.
Removing the Chairman now sends 2 messages:
• To the people: "We will not tolerate corruption"
• To politicians: "Fall in line, or you’re next" 
4. WHAT HAPPENS TO THE PEOPLE?
While leaders fight over power and party, Sagbama roads, schools, and primary health centers suffer.
LGs are supposed to be closest to the people. But they’ve become the ATM and punishment unit for state politics.
THE BIG QUESTION:
Is this removal about •accountability or control?
If it’s accountability, then publish the audit report. Prosecute. Recover funds.
If it’s control, then Bayelsa people should prepare — because no LGA Chairman is safe when politics shifts.
Bayelsa deserves LGAs that work, not LGAs that are used.
Until we respect LG autonomy, every 4 years we’ll keep seeing the same cycle: Probe. Remove. Appoint Caretaker. Repeat.
What do you think? Should the Assembly have this power? Or is this pure abuse?

”50 Shades of Homelessness in San Francisco...” Silicon Valley can build. Cars drive themselves around San Francisco. Founders are discussing Mars.
Meanwhile, another founder is sleeping in a Toyota Corolla explaining:
“We’re just being extremely capital efficient right now.”
I started ranking the housing situations.
Because when reality becomes absurd enough, your sarcasm reaches unexpected heights exactly when your housing situation reaches unexpected bottoms.
So here is the completely unofficial, politically incorrect, tragically realistic 50 Shades of Homelessness in San Francisco.
So... let’s play San Francisco unicorns – future billionaires – making-the-world-a-better-place – dreamers!
50 = Housing has defeated you.
0 = You have defeated housing.
Let's start!
50 — Rock bottom.
Concrete mattress. Urine. Weed. Garbage. Rats. Mystery liquid.
You own nothing, rent nothing, have nowhere to go…
and somehow somebody can still tell you to leave.
Even rock bottom has a checkout time.
42 — Toyota Corolla: 1 bedroom, 0 bathroom
Bedroom. Closet. Transportation. Occasionally dining room.
Bathroom?
Gym membership.
Congratulations.
You invented plumbing.
41 — Founder Car Edition™
MacBook. Pitch deck. YC application. AWS credits. $17 in checking.
You are not sleeping in your car.
You are:
EXTENDING RUNWAY.
Very different.
34 — Coworking-space amphibian
Your startup has an office.
Its founder does not have a bedroom.
Security:
“Did you sleep here?”
You:
“No. I was thinking horizontally.”
Very Silicon Valley.
33 — Hacker House:
17 laptops.
11 humans.
6 mattresses.
The room smells like generational shoes.
$300 in supplements.
Zero vegetables.
Everyone calls it:
“Community.”
Because “overpriced adult dorm with a deploy happening in the kitchen” sounds less investable.
Then we enter the hostel ecosystem.
31 — The Hostel From Hell™ !!!
Bed. Roof. Wi-Fi. Shower. Technically.
You are simply living in a room that smells like humanity has been marinating there since 1998.
The bathroom contains:
Hair.
Something sticky.
Something brown.
Something that might once have been white.
You need:
Towel #1 — Body.
Towel #2 — Floor Defense System™
Because if your naked foot touches that floor…
you do NOT wash it.
No!
You amputate the leg! Cut it off!!!!
Throw the entire thing in the garbage!
I don’t want it anymore!!!
Your suitcase is locked underneath somebody else’s bunk.
So every morning a curtain flies open:
“SHUT UP, BRO! I’M STILL TRYING TO SLEEP!!!”
Good morning, San Francisco!
Twenty minutes later you’re outside:
Founder breakfast.
Startup event.
Hackathon.
Looking completely normal.
Nobody knows you were just drying tomorrow’s underwear with somebody else’s hairdryer.
From the outside:
“You’re killing it in San Francisco!”
From the inside:
You’re calculating which towel is legally permitted to touch which surface.

The holy days are approaching — a special time when every Jew seeks to begin a new chapter, to be inscribed for a good and sweet year, and to enter Yom Kippur with Teshuvah, prayer, and charity.

The custom of Kaparot is an ancient Jewish tradition observed by many communities. The Rema refers to it as an established custom and mentions the practice of redeeming the Kaparot with money and giving the funds to charity.

(Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 605)

What is the meaning of Pidyon Kaparot?

Pidyon Kaparot does not replace Teshuvah, prayer, or improving one’s actions. Its purpose is to awaken the heart, inspire repentance and charity, and ask Hashem to bring us from judgment to mercy, from difficulty to salvation, and from darkness to light.

The Mishnah Berurah explains that this custom is meant to inspire a person to reflect on their deeds, return in Teshuvah, and pray that Hashem remove harsh decrees.

In the days before Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, we pray for life, health, livelihood, Shalom Bayit, worthy matches, joy from our children, protection, and salvation.
